paper_title: Probing the Blue Axion with Cosmic Optical Background Anisotropies
notes: Paper derives new bounds on decaying 'blue axion' (m_a ~ 5-25 eV, extended down to ~2.7 eV in note added) from HST 606 nm cosmic optical background anisotropy measurements, plus projections for 438/336 nm and LIM (HETDEX). Main exclusion curves are shown in Figs. 1, 8, 9 as lifetime/decay-rate (Gamma_a->gamma gamma in s^-1) or coupling g_agamma vs mass, but numerical curve values are not tabulated. The only explicit numerical limit in the text is from the Note Added: for m_a = 4.2 eV, Gamma > 3.03e-25 s^-1 excluded, corresponding to g_agamma > 2.33e-11 GeV^-1 (95% CL), the strongest bound in the MUSE gap m_a = 4.15-4.27 eV. Best-fit analysis at m_a = 10 eV suggests limits near ~1e-11 GeV^-1 scale for CDM. This is a cosmological (decaying relic) bound, not a haloscope DM density assumption; abundance assumed is cosmological Omega_CDM h^2 = 0.12 for the CDM case.
